butterfly_models.nearest_real_butterfly: realistic scale models (core/butterfly.py: disorder, tilt, diffraction, melanin backing/absorption; approximate)

findings: No phoneme class is limited to one or two colours: with every frame and 5 viewing angles the classes give 39–85 distinct colours (CIEDE2000 clusters ≤ 10), so no 'few colours' proof is claimed. Tilting the film from 0° to 60° alone multiplies the colours: per class, item × angles gives 3–23 distinct colours.

17 135 film colours of the main view were checked for validity and all come from physically realizable films (indices 1–2.5, |k| < 1, R + T = 1 checked); 8 995 of them are distinct display colours plotted in the class gamuts. The ideal-film views are not realizable (indices up to 57513).

One film per phoneme at normal incidence: the 14 vowels give 9 distinct colours and the 9 fricatives 7, but the 3 nasals collapse to 1 (magenta) and the 2 modelled affricates to 1 (both built mostly from ʃ). This is an observation, not a 'few' verdict: frames and angles spread the nasals to 56 colours, and no proof is claimed.

The most butterfly-like phoneme films: [z] (fricative) ρ = +0.98, [s] (fricative) ρ = +0.87, [f] (fricative) ρ = +0.75, [θ] (fricative) ρ = +0.69 (reflectance correlation with the nearest Morpho-/Beetle-like film, 380–780 nm; [z] also ΔE00 = 2.6). The match is in spectral SHAPE and hue only: [z] reflects at most R = 0.18, the butterfly film 0.91. Vowels, nasals and plosives are not (median ρ over all phonemes +0.13); the closest film by colour is a median ΔE00 = 15 away (these are idealised 1-D stacks). Against the realistic scale models (disorder, tilt, melanin absorption; approximate) the most frequent nearest species is Chrysochroa fulgidissima (22/43); the best match is [z] vs Morpho didius (ρ = +0.70, ΔE00 = 30), median ρ -0.26: the realistic, broader and dimmer spectra resemble phoneme films less than the idealised stacks do.
But every phoneme colour has a butterfly-material twin: an 8-layer chitin/air stack matches the absolute reflected colour to median ΔE00 = 0 (max 5.2; 42/43 below 2).

Voices: the butterfly whose all-pole voice is closest to most phonemes is Goupillaud speaker #3 (14/43; a random equal-thickness Garden film, not an insect); /s/ sounds most like Morpho-like (LSD 9.4 dB); all LSDs 3.1–23.1 dB.

Fluorescence (approximate, papiliochrome-type dye in every layer): under blacklight all 43 phoneme films glow the same green (max pairwise ΔE00 1.3, emission peak 503–510 nm) — a 'few colours' result with a proof: the film only multiplies the fixed emission band by an escape factor η ∈ [0.31, 0.51]. In daylight the dye adds 11–79 % of the luminance and the colours stay distinct.

Modelled items (e ɛ o from Hillenbrand means; ʒ tʃ dʒ from relatives) and the fallback plosives p b t d (context vowel averaged in) are approximations; the all-pole film is an envelope model for nasals, fricatives and plosives.

fluorescence_proof.title: Blacklight: why every phoneme film glows the same green
fluorescence_proof.claim: Under UV-A every realizable phoneme film shows ONE colour: the film cannot change the fluorophore's emission band, only multiply it by an escape factor with bounded log-slope κ, which moves the peak by at most σ²·κ and the colour by ΔE00 ≤ 1.3.
steps: Source term. Under the 365 nm LED the light leaving the film is L(λ) = R(λ)·I(λ) + QY·N_abs·e(λ)·η(λ)/λ (core/fluorescence.py, energy units). I(λ) sits below 380 nm where the CIE colour-matching functions are ≈ 0, so the reflected part carries a negligible share of Y (fluorescence share ≥ 0.9997 for every item). The UV colour is therefore the colour of S(λ) = e(λ)·η(λ)/λ alone.

Brightness drops out. QY·N_abs is one number per film (absorption changes how MUCH light is emitted, not WHERE in the spectrum); the displayed colour is exposure-normalised, so only the shape of S matters.

The emission is fixed by the fluorophore: e(λ) is a split Gaussian, peak λ0 = 505 nm, σ_b = 25 nm (blue side), σ_r = 50 nm (red side). The film cannot move it; it only multiplies it by the escape factor η(λ) = P_top/(P_top + P_bottom) ∈ (0, 1).

η is bounded for realizable films. With indices n ∈ [1, 2.5] a single interface reflects at most |r| = (2.5 − 1)/(2.5 + 1) ≈ 0.43, so neither side is a broadband mirror; over the emission window W = 430–655 nm (λ0 − 3σ_b … λ0 + 3σ_r) the computed η of all 43 films lies in [0.31, 0.51], and per film ρ_i = max η_i / min η_i ≤ 1.64.

Lemma (peak shift). Let S(λ) = exp(−(λ − λ0)²/2σ²)·w(λ) with w > 0 differentiable and κ = max_W |d ln w/dλ|. At an interior maximum λ* ∈ W, 0 = d ln S/dλ = −(λ* − λ0)/σ² + (ln w)′(λ*), hence |λ* − λ0| = σ²·|(ln w)′(λ*)| ≤ σ²·κ. For the split Gaussian ln e is C¹ at λ0, so the same holds with σ = σ_r if λ* > λ0 and σ = σ_b otherwise.

The maximum lies in W. Outside W, e(λ) ≤ e^(−4.5)·e(λ0) ≈ 0.011·e(λ0) and η ≤ 1, while e(λ0)·η(λ0) ≥ 0.31·e(λ0) inside, so the global peak of e·η is in W. Applying the lemma with w = η_i (photon spectrum) gives λ*_i ∈ [λ0 − σ_b²κ_i, λ0 + σ_r²κ_i].

Chromaticity. Each tristimulus value is T = ∫ c̄(λ)·e(λ)·η_i(λ)/λ dλ with c̄ ≥ 0. Since η_i ∈ [m_i, M_i] on W (where ≥ 99.7 % of the emission lies), X, Y and Z are each the flat-η reference value times a factor in [m_i, M_i]; therefore X/Y and Z/Y differ from the reference by a factor in [1/ρ_i, ρ_i] (up to e^(±0.02) for the 0.3 % tail outside W, since 0.003/η_min < 0.01 per value). This bound is loose (η varies slowly and the same factor enters numerator and denominator), and the true shifts are far smaller.

Conclusion. A realizable phoneme film only re-weights a fixed emission band by a slowly varying factor, so the blacklight colour is the fluorophore's colour, the same green for every phoneme. In daylight the film's own reflection is added and the colours differ again (see fluorescence.items[].hex_D65).
fluorescence_proof.numeric_check: 43 items: peak λ* ∈ [503, 510] nm; max |λ* − λ0| = 5 nm, every one ≤ its bound σ²κ_i + 1 nm (bounds 2–37 nm, κ_i ≤ 0.0165 /nm): True.
